blindSummary:
This is a self-governing overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state. Same-sex civil partnerships are legal (2020, after litigation); there is no legal gender recognition; the economy is tourism-dependent; the administering power's bathroom-policy machinery does not extend here, and the society is socially conservative.

The evidence base for this territory is partly shared with that of its administering power, adjusted for the local deviations noted above.
blindOutOfScope: A dependent territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations are noted in the summary.

NOTE: a further report on the same prison-housing litigation in a constituent nation of the administering power (Feb 2026), not about this territory; metropolitan-context material only.

LGBTQ news outlet (Aug 2009): legislators of the administering power criticised this territory's draft constitution for deliberately omitting sexual orientation as a prohibited discrimination ground - the relevant parliamentary committee called the omission 'deplorable' and warned it might leave residents with less than the full protection of the regional human-rights convention; the omission was at the islanders' behest.
Same article as above (alternate canonical link): legislators of the administering power criticise this territory's draft constitution for excluding gay rights from its non-discrimination grounds.

Local news service (July 2021): around 600 people - including the premier, the administering power's appointed governor, ministers and legislators - joined this territory's first Pride parade, organised by a local LGBTQ foundation - a historic milestone with official support; participants were asked to refrain from excessive displays of affection.
